Quarterly Reports

4 analyst reports · 1 story

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

FDJ United

A clean miss and the third guidance cut of 2026: Q3 revenue fell 8.1% to €794m (~$889m), ~5% below the ~€839m (~$940m) consensus, and the FY26 outlook moved to a mid-single-digit revenue decline, low-single-digit GGR decline and a ~23% recurring EBITDA margin (from 24.5% in February). Unlike Q1/Q2, the Q3 deterioration was not tax-driven (only ~€10m of incremental levies landed in the quarter) — it was the French lottery (draw games -17%), a ~80% retail sports payout and ~10% lower point-of-sale traffic, which makes the "defensive lottery" leg of the thesis look less defensive just as the online leg (UK GGR -24%) remains structurally impaired.

€1,950m (~$2.18bn)Q3 GGR-6.1% YoY / -8.8% QoQ

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

Sands China Ltd

A volume-and-share quarter that did not reach the P&L. Sands China grew gaming volumes in every segment (rolling +31%, non-rolling drop +11%, slot/ETG handle +26% YoY) and lifted mass GGR share to 26.1% – its best since Q4-23 – yet luck-adjusted EBITDA of $518m was -13.5% YoY and flat QoQ, because Londoner's premium-mass hold collapsed 480bps and the cost base is now ~$100m/quarter heavier. The reported +23% QoQ EBITDA rebound to $529m is almost entirely hold normalisation; shares fell 4.5% to a fresh 52-week low of HK$10.86 (~$1.39).

27.3%Adj. EBITDA margin-420bps YoY / +330bps QoQ

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence high

Betsson AB

Record revenue (EUR 326.5m / ~$366m, +10% reported, +8% organic, 4% above consensus) bought with a structurally lower margin: gross margin -870bps to 55.5% as regulated LatAm B2C casino replaced high-margin B2B licence income, leaving EBIT -31% and EPS -44% YoY. The second straight sequential EBIT rise and a +11% start to Q4 are real, but the earnings base has reset and the balance sheet is quietly thinning (net cash EUR 98m vs EUR 220m) with the buyback spent at SEK 112 against a SEK 95 share price.

EUR 326.5m (~$366m)Revenue (Q3-26)+10.4% YoY reported; +8.1% organic; +5.3% QoQ
EUR 63.4m (~$71m) / 19.4%EBITDA / margin-23.2% YoY; margin -850bps YoY, +60bps QoQ

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence high

Las Vegas Sands Corp.

A clean miss driven by the high end not showing up in either Singapore or Macao: net revenue -3.5% YoY to $3.22bn and adj. property EBITDA -16.7% to $1.12bn, ~13-14% below consensus on a hold-adjusted basis, with group margin -555bps to 34.8% as Macao opex was held flat sequentially into weaker premium spend and MBS mass hold collapsed to 18.7%. Management is doubling down rather than retrenching — $950m of buybacks (19% of the share count retired in 12 quarters), a 20% dividend hike for 2027, and no cuts to the Macao opex base or the $8bn MBS expansion — so the equity case is now a bet on the premium customer returning before leverage and payout optics become a constraint.

Market report · AUGUST 2026 · Confidence medium

Arizona

August 2026 was Arizona's softest month of the year: handle $582.8m (−4.6% YoY, −2.8% MoM), gross hold back to ~8.7% from an unusually book-friendly 10.1% a year earlier, and state privilege fees down 12% to ~$3.6m — a reminder that a 10%-of-adjusted-receipts, promo-deductible regime yields the state only ~0.6% of handle. Structurally nothing moved: a 99.7% mobile market, FanDuel/DraftKings holding 60% of handle (top four 82%), licence access gated through tribes or pro-sports franchises, and a governor who has already put a 45% rate for scale operators on the table.

Market report · 2026 · Confidence medium

Latin America

Latin America in 2026 is no longer one growth story. Brazil — the region's largest regulated market at BRL 37bn (~$7.1bn) GGR in 2025 and BRL 20.07bn (~$3.9bn, +15% YoY) in H1-26 — has been switched off by Provisional Measure 1.394/2026 since 6 October, and Lula's re-election on 25 October removes the quickest political route back. The five remaining markets now diverge on maturity rather than size: Colombia (regulated since 2016, 21 online operators, online VAT struck down in April), Peru (cleanest framework, but ISC-on-stakes risk of 1%→5%), Mexico (scale under a 1947 law with a 50% headline IEPS), Argentina (~50% offshore, acquisition-only entry) and Chile (bill still in Congress, framework 2027-28 at best).

Market report · 9M 2026 · Confidence medium

Maryland

Maryland is a mature, almost entirely mobile (98%+) sports-betting market that is still compounding volume — 9M 2026 handle $4,983.7m, +9% YoY, Q3 +11.4% — but gross win has decoupled from stakes: Q3 GGR fell 6.4% to $159.2m on a 9.9% hold and September GGR fell 20% at a 9.0% hold, so state receipts dropped 17.5% in Q3 despite the 20% mobile rate introduced in July 2025. The regulatory direction is toward higher fiscal extraction and perimeter defence (prediction markets, unlicensed online gaming) rather than product expansion, with iGaming still unlegalised and six land-based casinos flat-to-down (Q3 GGR $469.3m, −4%).

Market report · SEPTEMBER 2026 · Confidence medium

Ivory Coast

Côte d'Ivoire is a fast-growing (~XOF 706bn / ~$1.26bn licensed-sector turnover in 2024, +20.5% YoY) but structurally closed market: every online vertical – sports betting, online casino, virtuals – sits inside LONACI's exclusive State concession, and the 17 private brands on the ARJH register (up from 3 in Dec 2023) trade only as LONACI agrément-holders. September 2026 crystallised the tension in that model: national search demand rose 21.7% MoM and 12.6% YoY, Betclic took 55.2% of it, and the concessionaire's own online brand slipped to 6%. For an entrant the question is not 'can we get a licence' but 'can we secure a LONACI agrément on economics that survive a 5% online tax, 30% corporate tax, a 7.5% player-winnings withholding and a regulator that is visibly hardening enforcement (USSJH decree, April 2026).'

Virginia

September 2026 confirms Virginia's land-based casino market has re-based to a ~$1.2bn annualised AGR run-rate: five casinos won $97.6m (+33.5% YoY, flat MoM) with Caesars Danville (+28% YoY) and the Petersburg temporary Live! (opened Jan-26) doing the heavy lifting, while the two older permanent properties grew only mid-single digits and the state took $20.66m (21.2% effective) in graduated AGR tax. Online sports betting — the only digital vertical, taxed at 15% of AGR with 11 mobile permit-holders — is decelerating (August handle +4.3% YoY vs +22% a year earlier; hold 8.9%), and the big regulatory swing factors (iGaming, skill games, a Northern Virginia casino, the 2027 permanent openings in Norfolk and Petersburg) remain unresolved under the new Spanberger administration.

Colorado

August 2026 was Colorado's first sub-$400m month of the year: handle $388.1m (−7.0% YoY, −20.2% MoM), hold compressed to 8.49%, GGR $32.95m and state tax $3.15m (−14.9% YoY) — the regulator's "+20%" headline refers to fiscal-year-to-date tax, not the month. With the free-bet deduction now effectively nil (tax base ≈ GGR less 0.25% federal excise) and new deposit/marketing restrictions live since 12 Aug 2026, Colorado has moved from a growth market to a mature, 99.5%-online, tighter-margin market in which the NFL season and the prediction-market leak will decide whether FY2027 holds the FY2026 record ($6.4bn handle, >$47m tax).

Market report · SEPTEMBER 2026 · Confidence medium

Kansas

September 2026 confirms Kansas as a small, mature, structurally low-yield regulated market: sportsbook handle fell for a third straight YoY reading (-5.9% to $267.0m) while a still-thin 4.58% hold lifted taxable net revenue 48.7% to $12.2m and the state's 10% cut to just $1.2m — under half a cent per dollar wagered. Land-based GGR grew 3.8% to $34.4m and lottery sales 6% to $46.5m on iLottery, but the real story is regulatory: the 2025 contract-renewal moratorium has lapsed, Boot Hill/DraftKings have already locked in to 2030, and the 2027 session is the last window for legislators who want a larger take before all remaining sportsbook contracts expire on 31 Aug 2027.

New Jersey

September 2026 confirms New Jersey's structural bifurcation: iGaming win rose 13.0% to $274.8m and for a second straight month out-earned the nine Atlantic City floors ($227.8m, -1.3%), while online sports GGR fell 18.8% on a 1.3% football hold and FanDuel's lead over DraftKings collapsed from $15m to $3.4m. Mississippi

September 2026 was a good month for a flat market: Mississippi's commercial casinos won $195.6m (+4.5% YoY), driven entirely by the Gulf Coast (+7.7%) and a table-games hold bounce, while slots (+2.4%) merely stabilised and the river markets kept shrinking. The structural story is unchanged — a $2.4bn, 100% land-based, retail-only market whose sports book just posted a $34.0m handle (-12.9%) at a 10.6% hold, taxed at ~12% of GGR, and whose Senate killed statewide mobile wagering (HB 4074) for a third straight session; for an online-led operator the only addressable route in remains a casino partnership option on legislation that has not yet passed.

Market report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

Africa

Africa has no pan-continental GGR print; the Q3-26 "release" is a demand index (Blask, 42 markets) showing the continent down 1.9% QoQ with West Africa (Nigeria +15.6%, Ghana +21.5%) rebounding and the tail (Mali −80.8%, Rwanda −56.1%) collapsing. The only audited benchmark, South Africa, is a R74.5bn (~$4.07bn) GGR market growing 25.6% on online betting alone, while the rules elsewhere are moving toward higher fixed licence costs (Kenya KES 50m/~$388k online licence, 1-year term), broader stake/deposit-based excises (Kenya 5% of deposits, Tanzania 5% of stakes), player withholding (Kenya 20%) and payment-rail enforcement. Entry economics are deteriorating faster than demand is growing in most jurisdictions except South Africa and Nigeria.

Louisiana

September 2026 was Louisiana's best handle month of the year at $405.1m (+0.9% YoY), but a soft 10.7% hold cut net proceeds 8.0% to $43.4m and state tax 9.4% to $8.9m — the sportsbook market is now mature, 95% mobile, parlay-dependent (63% of mobile win) and taxed at 21.5%. The land-based base is the growth story for once ($195.5m casino GGR, +11.8% on landside relocations and Caesars New Orleans), while the rule-set is hardening: sweepstakes are banned with racketeering exposure from 1 Aug 2026, and a prop/micro-bet ban was shelved only because it would cost the state >$20m a year.
